content.text: I fixed the bug in `src/`, but I could not run the test suite or the two reported examples. The folder has no `node_modules`, and my attempt to run the source directly with Node was blocked by a permission prompt. The fix is verified by reading the code only. **Cause:** `Lexer.ts` builds `maskedSrc`, a copy of the source used to find emphasis delimiters. It first masks every escape (`\` followed by punctuation) with `+` characters. In `` `C:\Users\` `` the final `\` is followed by the closing backtick, so that backtick got masked too. The later code-span mask (`blockSkip`) then could not see the real end of the code span. It paired the opening backtick of `` `C:\Users\` `` with the one in `` `D:\` ``, which hid `**home**` inside a fake code span. **Fix:** - `src/rules.ts`: added an exported `escapeOutsideCodeSpan` regex. It matches a whole code span first, then falls back to the existing escape pattern. Code spans are left unchanged, so their backslashes and closing backtick are no longer masked. - `src/Lexer.ts`: imports that regex and uses it in place of `this.tokenizer.rules.inline.anyPunctuation` in the escape-masking step. A match that starts with a backtick is kept as-is, and everything else is masked with the same length-preserving `+` as before. Two notes: - I kept the escape mask ahead of the link and other masks on purpose. Reordering them would change how `\]` inside link text is matched. - Because the regex scans left to right, an escaped backtick such as `` \`x` `` is still treated as an escape, not as the start of a code span. Please run the test suite to confirm nothing else changed. The two examples from the report should now produce `home` and `b`.

result: I fixed the bug in `src/`, but I could not run the test suite or the two reported examples. The folder has no `node_modules`, and my attempt to run the source directly with Node was blocked by a permission prompt. The fix is verified by reading the code only. **Cause:** `Lexer.ts` builds `maskedSrc`, a copy of the source used to find emphasis delimiters. It first masks every escape (`\` followed by punctuation) with `+` characters. In `` `C:\Users\` `` the final `\` is followed by the closing backtick, so that backtick got masked too. The later code-span mask (`blockSkip`) then could not see the real end of the code span. It paired the opening backtick of `` `C:\Users\` `` with the one in `` `D:\` ``, which hid `**home**` inside a fake code span. **Fix:** - `src/rules.ts`: added an exported `escapeOutsideCodeSpan` regex. It matches a whole code span first, then falls back to the existing escape pattern. Code spans are left unchanged, so their backslashes and closing backtick are no longer masked. - `src/Lexer.ts`: imports that regex and uses it in place of `this.tokenizer.rules.inline.anyPunctuation` in the escape-masking step. A match that starts with a backtick is kept as-is, and everything else is masked with the same length-preserving `+` as before. Two notes: - I kept the escape mask ahead of the link and other masks on purpose. Reordering them would change how `\]` inside link text is matched. - Because the regex scans left to right, an escaped backtick such as `` \`x` `` is still treated as an escape, not as the start of a code span. Please run the test suite to confirm nothing else changed. The two examples from the report should now produce `home` and `b`.
